text: Rigor is kindness to your future self: state assumptions, check units, and make the result falsifiable.
author: Daily note

text: If you can’t describe what would change your mind, you’re not doing science yet.
author: Daily note

text: A detector is a translator: nature speaks in interactions; we answer in signals and uncertainties.

text: Good reconstruction is calibrated humility: model the systematics as carefully as the central value.
author: Daily note

text: Simulation earns trust only after it survives comparison to reality—again and again.
author: Daily note

text: Chase clarity: a clean plot with honest errors beats a complicated story every time.
author: Daily note

text: Every pipeline is an experiment. Version it, test it, and make it reproducible.
author: Daily note

text: Hardware constrains what you can measure; analysis constrains what you can claim.

text: When results disagree, first suspect definitions, units, selections, and calibrations.

text: Your best ally against bias is a pre-defined comparison and a transparent uncertainty budget.

text: Physics rewards patient iteration: build, measure, learn, and rebuild.
author: Daily note

text: The most dangerous number is one without an error bar.
author: Daily note

text: A beautiful idea becomes science when it meets a quantitative test.
author: Daily note

text: In high-multiplicity environments, your real enemy is ambiguity—fight it with timing and geometry.
author: Daily note

text: If the plot looks too perfect, audit the selection and the defaults.
author: Daily note

text: Optimization without validation is just wishful thinking with extra steps.
author: Daily note

text: A good notebook tells a story; a good repository tells the truth reproducibly.
author: Daily note

text: Instruments are arguments made of metal, silicon, gas, and code.
author: Daily note

text: Measure twice: once for the value, once for the systematics.
author: Daily note

text: When in doubt, reduce the problem until you can test one knob at a time.
